### National rollout step 556: San Agustin priority range and authority triage — 5 November 2026

Compared three high-priority survey labels with independent range references. *Pomatoschistus minutus* is documented from the eastern Atlantic through European waters; *Strongylura marina* is documented in the Western Atlantic; and *Tetraodon lineatus* is documented from North and Central Africa. These ranges make each reported Romblon label a substantial identification question, but do not prove absence or rule out a stray or introduction.

Found a useful qualification for *T. lineatus*: the 1999 BFAR *Common and Local Names of Marine Fishes of the Philippines* lists it with local name “Coral butterfly” in a Palawan name list. The book's methods describe collecting common/local names through illustrated forms with fishers and market vendors, plus institutional information; it does not provide a voucher for the 2022 Romblon survey. The historical Philippine name-use entry therefore cannot resolve specimen identity or establish an occurrence.

Added `mimaropa-san-agustin-priority-range-authority-triage-20261105.json` and one source-registry entry; registry total: 705. Linked the existing BFAR reference to this review. No occurrence, species-by-waterbody row, geometry, absence claim, or public-app data was added; no contact was sent.

See the [Naturalis specialist account](https://fishes-fnam.linnaeus.naturalis.nl/linnaeus_ng/app/views/species/taxon.php?epi=141&id=109417), [Catalog of Fishes on *Strongylura marina*](https://researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/ichthyology/catalog/fishcatget.asp?genus=Strongylura&tbl=species), [Catalog of Fishes on *Tetraodon lineatus*](https://researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/ichthyology/catalog/fishcatget.asp?genus=Tetraodon&tbl=species), the [1999 BFAR reference](https://repository.nfrdi.da.gov.ph/items/0bc0e276-842e-470a-911d-182f97baf0a3/full), and the [triage artifact](data/research/philippines/mimaropa-san-agustin-priority-range-authority-triage-20261105.json).

**Next:** screen the remaining 36 article labels for geographic outliers and current accepted combinations; preserve unresolved source spellings and request no public occurrence projection without specimen evidence.

### National rollout step 557: San Agustin range-authority discrepancy follow-up — 5 November 2026

Reviewed two more Table 1 names against taxonomic revisions and Philippine specimen/barcode context. A 2023 integrative revision narrows Hypseleotris cyprinoides to the western Indian Ocean and nearby regions, while a 2005 museum-based paper lists named Philippine lots and a 2025 North Luzon barcode dataset reports voucher-linked H. cyprinoides sequences. The latter paper's sample-level supplement was blocked by a browser check, and the sequences were not re-evaluated under the 2023 species revision. This is a taxonomic/range-authority discrepancy that requires specimen and sequence review, not evidence of Philippine absence or a verified San Agustin occurrence.

For Eleotris mauritiana, the 2026 Catalog of Fishes lists the name as uncertain, while a 2019 molecular/morphological study treats it as the same species as E. acanthopoma and a 2025 North Luzon barcode dataset lists E. acanthopomus. These competing treatments and Philippine records under another name do not resolve the Romblon specimen. Keep the survey's printed form and seek its voucher before any reassignment.

Added the research-only review artifact and one source-register entry; registry total: 711. Six range-mismatch labels remain in the voucher queue; three labels now have separate authority/range discrepancies; 16 of 39 names have been screened and 23 remain. No occurrence, waterbody, geometry, diet, legal, safety or public-app rows were added; no contact was sent. The North Luzon paper is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; no table, supplement, sequence, or image was copied.

See the [2023 Hypseleotris revision](https://academic.oup.com/zoolinnean/article/198/4/1035/7150892), [2005 Australian Museum revision](https://journals.australian.museum/media/Uploads/Journals/18010/1436_complete.pdf), [2025 North Luzon barcode dataset](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12475234/), [2019 Eleotris study](https://doi.org/10.1111/zsc.12366), and [research review](../data/research/philippines/mimaropa-san-agustin-range-authority-followup-2-20261105.json).

**Next:** continue screening the remaining 23 labels; after the name/range pass, seek the RSU voucher/accession crosswalk and resolve the article's conflicting locality text and unnamed reach stations before considering any occurrence rows.

### National rollout step 558: San Agustin Awaous range-authority follow-up — 5 November 2026

No new range-authority conflict was found for *A. interrupta*.

A separate 2026 integrative paper reports Panay River paratypes of the distinct species *A. maculatus*. Those vouchers provide Philippine Awaous comparison material, but do not permit relabeling the unexamined Romblon specimen.

### National rollout step 559: San Agustin *Butis* and milkfish range-authority follow-up — 5 November 2026

Screened *Butis amboinensis* and *Chanos chanos*. The current Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes (online version updated 10 June 2026) treats *B. amboinensis* as valid and includes the Philippines in its Indo-West Pacific range; it also treats *B. leucurus*, described from Negros with holotype USNM 51953, as a synonym. The latter historical type-locality evidence remains qualified because an earlier synonymy citation is marked with question. GBIF's exact accepted species-name match places *B. amboinensis* in Eleotridae, while the current specialist Catalog places it in Butidae. This is a higher-classification difference, not a range mismatch or identification of the San Agustin fish.

FAO's *Chanos chanos* species profile describes the broad tropical range and juvenile movement through mangroves, estuaries, coastal lagoons, and sometimes freshwater lakes. Kumagai, Bagarinao and Unggui's 1985 study documents juvenile milkfish in a natural mangrove lagoon on Naburut Island, central Philippines. This separate historical study and national aquaculture context do not verify a wild Romblon population or identify the 2022 San Agustin survey specimens. Both source labels remain unresolved for voucher and station crosswalk; no occurrence assertion was added.

Added `mimaropa-san-agustin-range-authority-followup-4-20261105.json` and one source-registry entry; registry total: 713. Six voucher-priority range mismatches and four separate range-authority discrepancies remain. Twenty of 39 source labels have now been screened; 19 remain. No waterbody, geometry, diet, catchability, legal, safety, or public-app row was added, and no contact was sent.

See the [Catalog of Fishes on *B. amboinensis*](https://researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/ichthyology/catalog/fishcatget.asp?spid=18549), [Catalog's *B. leucurus* record](https://researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/ichthyology/catalog/fishcatget.asp?spid=48607), [FAO milkfish profile](https://www.fao.org/fishery/docs/CDrom/aquaculture/I1129m/file/en/en_milkfish.htm), [SEAFDEC/AQD repository record for the 1985 study](https://repository.seafdec.org.ph/handle/10862/1165?show=full), and [research review](../data/research/philippines/mimaropa-san-agustin-range-authority-followup-4-20261105.json).

### National rollout step 565: MIMAROPA Palawan river voucher and diet evidence review — 6 November 2026

Reviewed Cervancia and Kottelat's 2007 original description of the existing *Cyclocheilichthys schoppeae* freshwater candidate and compared its type-series account with Balisco and Liao's 2025 CC BY 4.0 checklist. The original paper reports freshwater collection from northern Palawan river basins and a three-fish gut-content sample containing shrimp, worms, insect larvae, detritus, and sand. Treat this only as a small source-specific natural-diet observation, not a complete diet or bait guide.

The article lists 16 paratypes but labels Table 1 as holotype plus 14 paratypes; it does not reconcile the difference. Babuyan appears in the distribution paragraph but not in the material examined list. Iwahig remains a conditional hypothesis about a 1963 fish the authors had not inspected. The 2025 checklist has a spelling variant and says WPU-PPC staff could not confirm deposition of the uncatalogued specimens. A search-indexed official IUCN result reports an Endangered assessment last assessed in 2020, but the assessment page returned 403; no fine-scale locality coordinates or map were copied. The 2007 article states copyright © National University of Singapore and no open license was verified.

Added the research review and one source-registry entry; total: 728. The existing candidate remains pending. No specimen identity, new occurrence, waterbody, geometry, public diet, safety, legal, or public-app row was approved, and no contact was sent.

See the [2007 original description](https://lkcnhm.nus.edu.sg/app/uploads/2017/06/55rbz141-145.pdf), the [2025 type checklist](https://doi.org/10.3897/zookeys.1246.145752), [Kottelat 2013](https://lkcnhm.nus.edu.sg/app/uploads/2017/04/rbz_S27.pdf), the [IUCN assessment record](https://doi.org/10.2305/IUCN.UK.2021-2.RLTS.T90999908A162164632.en), and [the review artifact](../data/research/philippines/mimaropa-palawan-cyclocheilichthys-schoppeae-river-voucher-diet-review-20261106.json).

### National rollout step 572: Historical fish records for Camp Balete, Rio Baco — 6 November 2026

Reviewed Jordan and Richardson's 1908 primary paper. It explicitly associates *Barbodes hemictenus*, *Kuhlia marginata*, and *Lutjanus argentimaculatus* with Camp Balete, Rio Baco, Mindoro. The source also reports *Ophiocara aporos* at the locality, but this name is held because the current-name crosswalk remains unresolved. The paper's introduction places the wider McGregor collection in a 1906 context; it does not assign a collection date to each Baco specimen. Although the *Barbodes hemictenus* account names type/cotype lots, it does not identify which lot was collected at Camp Balete; the other three passages provide no Baco catalog number. Added one research-only review and one registry entry; total: 735. No modern geometry, coordinates, app row, current-presence, diet, rules, safety, or catchability assertion was added.

See the [NOAA-hosted primary paper](https://spo.nmfs.noaa.gov/sites/default/files/pdf-content/fish-bull/fb27.8.pdf), the Catalog of Fishes' [*Barbodes hemictenus*](https://researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/ichthyology/catalog/fishcatget.asp?spid=31226) and [*Lutjanus argentimaculatus*](https://researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/ichthyology/catalog/fishcatget.asp?spid=15550) entries, GBIF's [*Kuhlia marginata*](https://www.gbif.org/taxon/3RFBY) entry, and the [review artifact](../data/research/philippines/mimaropa-baco-rio-baco-1908-fish-record-screen-20261106.json).

### National rollout step 580: Cagayan basin B0380 geometry and bounded GBIF locality screen — 6 November 2026

Checksum-verified the Zenodo basin shapefile and matched feature B0380, “Cagayan,” to its polygon. The feature is a northern Luzon drainage basin in WGS 84, with a six-part polygon; its bounding box is 121.528549–122.450000 E and 17.108333–18.596476 N. The identical name Cagayan de Misamis refers to a separate Mindanao locality. The polygon is research geometry only, not an administrative or municipal-water boundary.

A bounded GBIF coordinate screen covered the B0380 bounding box and all eight basin-candidate names. The strongest independent leads are a 2008 *Anguilla luzonensis* sequence accession whose one shared coarse coordinate falls inside the polygon, and Smithsonian holotype USNM 333262 for *Nomorhamphus rossi* with a textual Intel River/Baggao locality but no coordinate overlay. The eel's 36 GBIF feed rows reduce to 35 unique sequence accessions because AB469437 is duplicated across NCBI-mined and INSDC feeds; all 36 rows share one coordinate and none reports a catalog number or coordinate uncertainty. Two *Mugil cephalus* market-voucher catalog numbers are duplicated as six GBIF rows; vendor-vicinity text and generalized market coordinates do not establish exact catch points. The *Glossogobius biorbitalis* search yielded a higher-rank match only; a separate *G. giuris* market record is not a match for that species. Other zero/missing-rank results are bounded search outcomes, not evidence of absence. The *Neostethus villadolidi* type locality in Cagayan de Misamis, Mindanao, is a place-name ambiguity, not proof of absence from Luzon.

Added one geometry/locality review and two source-registry entries; registry total: 744. No basin polygon, species/occurrence row, diet, catchability, legal, safety, or app data was added; publication approval remains false. GBIF dataset metadata was last version-checked as v1.192 on 5 November 2026; occurrence screening was reviewed on 6 November.

See the [Zenodo basin dataset](https://zenodo.org/records/19511163), [GBIF occurrence API](https://techdocs.gbif.org/en/openapi/v1/occurrence), [DDBJ accession AB469437.1](https://getentry.ddbj.nig.ac.jp/getentry/na/AB469437/?filetype=html), [Smithsonian USNM 333262 catalog result](https://collections.si.edu/search/results.htm?q=%22Meisner%2C+A.%22), and the [review artifact](../data/research/philippines/national-freshwater-cagayan-b0380-geometry-gbif-locality-screen-20261106.json).

### National rollout step 583: *Stigmatogobius elegans* Imurung River type-series crosswalk — 6 November 2026

The original and museum locality names a river and Cagayan Province but provides no coordinates or explicit Cagayan River drainage link; membership in B0380 remains unresolved. The 2026 province-only observation is a separate research lead and not a map-ready or voucher-linked occurrence. The paper's “single river system” distribution statement is historical, not a current range assessment. No public species/occurrence, geometry, diet, catchability, legal, safety, or app row was added. Added two source-registry entries; registry total: 748. Publication approval remains false.

### National rollout step 592: Correctly filtered Region II river GBIF source crosswalk — 9 November 2026

The first exploratory GBIF request used the unsupported `class=Actinopterygii` parameter; GBIF ignored it, so its mixed-mammal/plant/insect rows and derived report were discarded as evidence. The rerun used the documented Catalogue of Life XR `taxonKey=8VR36` plus `checklistKey=7ddf754f-d193-4cc9-b351-99906754a03b`. Across 29 names and both `waterBody`/`locality` fields, 58 count queries returned four nonzero pairs (Cagayan River and Magat River); complete retrieval returned 32 query rows and 31 unique GBIF IDs.

Direct BOLD portal records resolve 12 historical 2011 process IDs from Cagayan River, Cagayan, to seven *Plicofollis magatensis* samples and five *Clarias macrocephalus* samples. BOLD reports morphology-based identification by Jonas P. Quilang and GenBank accessions; the DOST-published 2014 Philippine Journal of Science article provides independent catfish/voucher context. BOLD supplied no coordinate accuracy, so the sample sites remain text-only. Five CAS specimens name Magat River, Bayombong, Nueva Vizcaya, from 1931/1940 and four recorded taxa, but carry 3,257 m coordinate uncertainty. One Aparri/Cagayan record carries 50,479 m uncertainty and remains held. Nine apparent Cagayan River records are from Misamis Oriental; two Auburn records are adjacent Ifugao localities; one Cagayan/Philippine Sea row has conflicting fields; and one NHM row is genus-rank and undated. Those do not become Region II species rows.

The source registry now records the GBIF screen, BOLD/iBOL records, and primary study separately (834 registered sources). The review report contains query and source-response hashes, dataset DOIs/licenses, sequence-accession identifiers, and a coordinate-free candidate ledger. No species or occurrence rows, geometry, diet, catchability, access, legal, safety, or app claims were added; neither the historical evidence nor the CC BY 4.0 BOLD dataset metadata resolves rights for reusing the article.

See the [corrected count report](../data/research/philippines/national/reviews/gbif-region02-river-field-counts-col-filtered-20261109.json), [record-fetch report](../data/research/philippines/national/reviews/gbif-region02-river-record-candidate-review-col-filtered-20261109.json), [source crosswalk](../data/research/philippines/national/reviews/gbif-region02-river-candidate-source-review-20261109.json), the [BOLD Data Portal API](https://www.boldsystems.org/data/api/), and the [primary catfish study](https://philjournalsci.dost.gov.ph/molecular-phylogeny-of-catfishes-teleostei-siluriformes-in-the-philippines-using-the-mitochondrial-genes-coi-cyt-b-16s-rrna-and-the-nuclear-genes-rag1-and-rag2/).

**Next:** see step 593 for the completed specialist taxonomy pass. Continue source discovery for Region II inland and coastal waters without treating its bounded GBIF results as a checklist.

### National rollout step 593: Cagayan–Magat fish-name and family cross-check — 10 November 2026

Fetched seven direct Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes records (Catalog online version updated 20 October 2026): six names occurring in the corrected Region II candidate review and one related synonym/type-locality entry. Catalog current-name and family statements agree with the GBIF name/family for *Clarias macrocephalus*, *Plicofollis magatensis*, *Glossogobius celebius*, and *Zenarchopterus philippinus*. The Catalog confirms the name *Rhinogobius bucculentus* but places it in Oxudercidae: Gobionellinae, whereas the GBIF CAS rows use Gobiidae; preserve the family conflict. For the Magat CAS label *Liza melinopterus*, GBIF uses *Planiliza melinopterus*, WoRMS lists *Planiliza melinoptera*, and the current Catalog entry gives *Chelon melinopterus*. Keep the recorded label and hold a preferred display name pending expert resolution.

The Catalog lists *Zenarchopterus magatensis* as a synonym of *Z. philippinus* and gives its type series locality as branches of the Magat River and tributary creeks at Bagabag, Nueva Vizcaya. This is useful historical type-locality context, not an additional occurrence or a georeference for the separate 1931/1940 CAS voucher rows. The Catalog cross-check does not re-identify any specimens; the BOLD records remain 2011 source-reported localities without coordinate accuracy, while the five CAS Magat rows retain 3,257 m uncertainty. The Catalog says the Philippines is only a possible part of the distribution for *C. macrocephalus*, another reason to keep those records source-attributed rather than broadening the species range claim.

The review is in [the taxonomy crosswalk](../data/research/philippines/national/reviews/region02-cagayan-magat-fish-taxonomy-crosswalk-20261110.json); the reproducible request is `npm run species:national:gbif:region02-river-taxonomy-review`. Two source-registry entries record the Catalog pass and WoRMS name conflict; registry total is 836. No public species or occurrence rows, geometry, diet, catchability, access, rules, safety, or app claims were added; publication approval remains false.

See the [Catalog of Fishes](https://researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/ichthyology/catalog/), its direct records for [*Clarias macrocephalus*](https://researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/ichthyology/catalog/fishcatget.asp?spid=4662), [*Plicofollis magatensis*](https://researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/ichthyology/catalog/fishcatget.asp?spid=53678), [*Glossogobius celebius*](https://researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/ichthyology/catalog/fishcatget.asp?spid=18734), [the Magat mullet label](https://researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/ichthyology/catalog/fishcatget.asp?spid=33583), [*Rhinogobius bucculentus*](https://researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/ichthyology/catalog/fishcatget.asp?spid=43687), [*Zenarchopterus philippinus*](https://researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/ichthyology/catalog/fishcatget.asp?spid=31803), and [*Z. magatensis*](https://researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/ichthyology/catalog/fishcatget.asp?spid=45369); and the [WoRMS *Liza* name list](https://www.marinespecies.org/aphia.php?p=taxlist&tName=Liza).

### National rollout step 594: Review the Aparri fyke-net bycatch study and its reuse limits — 10 November 2026

Reviewed Casco et al. (2025), a primary study of weekly landed fyke-net catches from five glass-eel fishers at Toran, Aparri, sampled March–April 2023. The paper reports two target glass-eel taxa and 31 bycatch taxa (29 fish and two penaeid invertebrates); it used pigmentation/microscopy for glass eels and morphology for bycatch. This is a dated, gear-specific landing-site sample, not a complete or current Region II species list. Toran is the landing site, not an exact capture location for each fish, and the reviewed article provides no specimen voucher or sequence accessions.

The abstract reports 16 bycatch families, while a later results paragraph says 17 and includes Anguillidae, the target glass-eel family. Scientific-name spellings also vary between article sections. These source-internal issues need independent taxonomic and denominator review. The journal marks the article CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, so the article/table is registered as a research lead only; its species table was not copied into Bangwit data. No occurrence, public geometry, safety/legal advice, or app data was added. The existing Escaño et al. (2022) NFRDI/GenBank crosswalk was referenced rather than duplicated; it reports 25 retained *Cestraeus goldiei* sequences, including 24 Cagayan/Isabela samples and one Abra sample, with no coordinates and four previously documented Isabela locality conflicts.

See the [official journal article and license](https://li01.tci-thaijo.org/index.php/JFE/article/view/263039), the [full article PDF](https://li01.tci-thaijo.org/index.php/JFE/article/download/263039/179948/1087115), the [NFRDI article](https://doi.org/10.31398/tpjf/29.2.2022A0003), the existing [NFRDI/GenBank crosswalk](../data/research/philippines/national-ludong-2022-nfrdi-genbank-crosscheck-20261030.json), and the [new source review](../data/research/philippines/national/reviews/region02-aparri-fyke-glass-eel-bycatch-source-review-20261110.json). One new source-registry entry was added; registry total is 837. Publication approval remains false.

**Next:** prioritize separately licensed/open Region II surveys for rivers, lakes, reservoirs, lagoons, wetlands, and estuaries. Independently cross-check source-reported names and localities; do not project this CC BY-NC-ND table into the app.

### National rollout step 595: Add the Cagayan River glass-eel recruitment study — 10 November 2026

Reviewed the early-view full text of Aoyama et al. (2015), a monthly glass-eel recruitment study at the Cagayan River mouth. It reports five *Anguilla* labels among 32,178 sampled glass eels during May 2008–September 2009 and November 2011–December 2012. The second period has a one-month end-date discrepancy in the discussion. The authors explicitly warn that samples do not represent absolute recruitment abundance because monthly sample volumes varied with catches and prices. This is historical estuary recruitment evidence, not adult-fish distribution or a basin-wide freshwater checklist.

No coordinates or reusable collection boundary were extracted, no species/occurrence rows were added, and no app or current-abundance claim was approved. The public early-view PDF contains no identified article-specific reuse license; its accessibility is not treated as permission to reproduce the paper's tables or figures. The review and source registry now record the evidence and limits; registry total is 838.

See the [full-text PDF](https://pacificscience.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/10/pac-sci-early-view-69-2-8.pdf), the [DOI](https://doi.org/10.2984/69.2.8), the [journal information](https://uhpress.hawaii.edu/title/ps/), and the [research review](../data/research/philippines/national/reviews/region02-cagayan-estuary-aoyama-glass-eel-recruitment-review-20261110.json). ### National rollout step 596: Review the 2009 Cagayan glass-eel sample — 10 November 2026

Reviewed Yoshinaga et al. (2014), an open-access primary study under CC BY 2.0. Local fishers collected 767 glass eels with a set net at the Cagayan River estuary in Aparri on 26 January and 19 February 2009. The paper genetically verified all 52 specimens classified as *Anguilla japonica*; these were in the January catch, while none were identified in the February sample. A genetic subsample of 32 pigmented long-fin eels from the January sample identified *A. luzonensis* (4), *A. marmorata* (27), and *A. celebesensis* (1). These are subsample counts, not full catch totals. Thirty-one short-fin January specimens were attributed to *A. bicolor pacifica* using morphology and prior records, without reported genetic confirmation for those individuals.

This supports historical glass-eel evidence at a named estuary and collection dates, not adult freshwater distribution or the entire Cagayan basin. The study locator map does not give capture coordinates; no voucher/catalog IDs or GenBank accessions were found in the reviewed article. The February sample's zero is not treated as absence. No species/occurrence rows, geometry, or app claims were added, and publication approval remains false.

See the [publisher article and CC BY 2.0 statement](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/1810-522X-53-13), its [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1186/1810-522X-53-13), and the [research review](../data/research/philippines/national/reviews/region02-cagayan-estuary-yoshinaga-japanese-eel-review-20261110.json). One source-registry entry was added; registry total is 839.

**Next:** seek independently accessible, dated fish surveys for inland Cagayan basin waters and other Region II rivers, lakes, reservoirs, wetlands, estuaries, and brackish sites. Prioritize voucher or accession crosswalks. Separately pursue the full station, sample-date, and accession details of the official UPLB 2022 Cagayan eel study; do not treat its abstract-only source entry as species-level evidence.

### National rollout step 597: Review the UPLB Cagayan eel paper and GenBank sample crosswalk — 10 November 2026

Reviewed the official UPLB/PAS abstract and an author-uploaded full-text copy of Hilario et al. (2022), then retrieved the 63 sample-linked GenBank records. The paper reports 23 glass eels, 20 elvers, and 20 yellow eels sourced from the Cagayan River at Barangay Toran, Aparri, and sampled at the BFAR National Freshwater Fisheries Technology Center eel-culture facility. The article’s 2022 source labels total 8 *Anguilla bicolor pacifica* and 15 *A. marmorata* among glass eels; 10 *A. bicolor pacifica*, 8 *A. marmorata*, and 2 *A. luzonensis* among elvers; and 10 *A. bicolor pacifica* and 10 *A. marmorata* among yellow eels. The paper also documents morphology/genetics disagreement, including *A. marmorata* and *A. luzonensis* confusion.

GenBank accession annotations provide a crosswalk to isolates G1–G23, J1–J20, and A1–A20, with 2018 collection-date qualifiers of 12 February (23 glass eels), 27 April (20 elvers), and 30 August (20 yellow eels). The article does not state field sampling dates; these database dates remain accession-level metadata. None of the 63 records has a country, latitude/longitude, or specimen-voucher qualifier. The article names a source locality but supplies no capture coordinates, exact station, standardized effort, or basin-wide survey design.

Taxonomic concepts conflict: the paper uses *A. bicolor pacifica*, GenBank records use *A. pacifica*, the current Eschmeyer Catalog lists *A. pacifica* as valid, while WoRMS accepts *A. bicolor* and treats the trinomial as unaccepted; NCBI Taxonomy uses *A. pacifica* but disclaims authority for nomenclature. Preserve the source labels and do not harmonize them until a project taxonomy policy is selected. No species/occurrence rows, geometry, article tables/figures, or app content were added. Rights remain unverified because no article-specific reuse license was found; publication approval remains false. The existing source entry now records the full-text/accession review, and the registry total remains 839.

See the [official UPLB article page](https://pas.uplb.edu.ph/journal-issues/identification-of-tropical-freshwater-eels-anguilla-spp-in-cagayan-river-philippines/), the [author-uploaded full-text page](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364351531_Identification_of_Tropical_Freshwater_Eels_Anguilla_spp_in_Cagayan_River_Philippines), the [GenBank accession query](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nuccore/?term=MN080877%3AMN080899%5BAccession%5D+OR+MN150017%3AMN150056%5BAccession%5D), the [Eschmeyer Catalog record](https://researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/ichthyology/catalog/fishcatget.asp?spid=60817), the [WoRMS taxon record](https://www.marinespecies.org/aphia.php?id=293543&p=taxdetails), and the [research review](../data/research/philippines/national/reviews/region02-cagayan-river-hilario-eel-identification-review-20261110.json). The official PDF endpoint was inaccessible during this review; the ResearchGate copy is author-uploaded and not a verified reuse license.

**Next:** use the article’s accession list only as a research crosswalk; continue to source independently accessible, site-linked fish evidence across Cagayan Valley rivers, lakes, reservoirs, wetlands, estuaries, and brackish habitats. Prioritize records with explicit locations, collection dates, methods, vouchers or accessions, and reuse terms; keep shortfin-eel taxonomy unresolved at the app layer until the project selects an authority.
